title: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency & Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, and Compliance Evidence Workflows
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls across RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gates, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for engineering, security, and compliance stakeholders who are responsible for designing, operating, or auditing the platform.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood-hosted services (API control plane, serving runtime, observability stack), Dedicated control plane components, and Private deployment packaging where Redwood is the vendor. Excludes third-party SaaS products operated entirely by customers; those are covered by separate customer-acceptance and vendor-assessment contracts.

Owners and Contacts

- Document owner: Security (Evelyn Chen)
- Primary reviewers: Eng SRE (Samir Kapoor), Eng Platform (Lina Gomez), Product Security (Jordan Mills)
- On-call for evidence & audit requests: security-oncall@redwood.ai

1) RBAC and Authentication

Principles

- Least privilege by default: grant minimum permissions required for a role to perform duties.
- Role-based assignment: avoid individual permissions; prefer group/role bindings.
- Separation of duties: operational vs. change-management privileges are split.
- Time-bound elevated access: use just-in-time (JIT) access for emergency ops.

Role taxonomy (examples)

- security-admin (managed by Security): can manage IAM roles, view all audit logs, approve high-risk exceptions.
- infra-operator: manage cloud infra (network, VPCs), no production data access by default.
- runtime-operator: operate serving clusters, pod-level access; limited to non-PII datasets.
- app-developer: deploy application code, limited to deployment infra and CI artifacts.
- product-analytics: read-only access to aggregated metrics and non-sensitive telemetry.
- customer-support: access to support tools with session recording and time-limited elevated view of customer metadata (requires approval).

Access provisioning and review

1. Request: All role requests go through the internal IAM portal (Confluence link + SSO form). Provide justification, duration, and approver.
2. Approval: Role owners approve within 48 business hours. Emergency approvals use the JIT flow and must be logged with a ticket.
3. Review cadence: Quarterly role membership review owned by Security and HR.
4. Deprovision: Offboarding workflow via HR integrations automatically triggers revocation within 4 hours of termination in 95% of cases.

Authentication and SSO

- Primary authentication: SAML 2.0 / OIDC via corporate identity provider (IdP).
- MFA: Required for all interactive access (TOTP + re-keying for highly privileged roles).
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS for cluster-internal components; short-lived service tokens (rotation every 24 hours) for cross-region control-plane calls.

Sample IAM policy snippet (pseudo-JSON for clarity):

- "effect": "allow", "action": ["s3:GetObject"], "resource": ["arn:redwood:logs:prod:*:audit/*"], "condition": {"StringEquals": {"redwood:role": "audit-reader"}}

2) Audit Logging

Goals and requirements

- Ensure tamper-evident, centralized logging for security-relevant events: authn/authz events, privilege changes, configuration changes, deployment approvals, and sensitive-data access.
- Maintain at least N+1 copies (primary index + immutable cold storage) for 365 days (see retention table below).
- Provide queryable logs for investigations with SLA for access.

Log sources

- Identity Provider (SSO): sign-in, MFA challenges, session terminations.
- IAM and RBAC changes: role creation, role binding changes, policy updates.
- Control plane API: deploys, config changes, model-version rollouts.
- Serving runtime: model load/unload, raw request metadata (no customer PII), token counts, error traces.
- Observability & tracing: sampling traces for latency/trace-level debug.
- Customer support sessions: session start/stop and snapshots (content redacted per retention rules).

Integrity and protection

- Logs are pushed to an immutable write-once store (WORM) with checksums.
- Stored copies are encrypted at rest using KMS-managed keys; key access is restricted to security-admins.
- Alerting on missing heartbeat (agent outage > 10 minutes) and abnormal log-volume drops (> 50% vs baseline).

Access and SLOs

- Log access request SLA: 24 hours for normal requests, 4 hours for incidents (security-oncall).
- Search/query SLA: ad-hoc queries up to 30 days retention returned within 2 hours for large scans; smaller queries (< 1M events) returned within 15 minutes.

3) Data Residency & Retention

Data residency by substrate

- Control plane metadata: replicated across US and EU regions depending on customer tenancy/contract. Customers in the EU may require EU-only control plane deployments under Private offering.
- Customer data (payloads/inputs): stored in region selected by customer; default region is US-WEST for hosted customers unless contract specifies otherwise.

Retention policy (representative)

- Audit logs (security-relevant): hot index 90 days, warm 275 days, cold/archival 365 days total.
- Support session recordings: 90 days (unless customer requires different retention).
- Raw request telemetry (non-PII aggregated metrics): 180 days.
- Model artifacts and container images: retained per release-policy (minimum 2 years for reproducibility).

Retention table (single-line CSV style)

"data_type,hot_days,warm_days,cold_days,total_days,owner"
"audit_logs,90,275,0,365,security"
"support_sessions,30,60,0,90,customer-support"
"telemetry_aggregates,90,90,0,180,observability"
"model_artifacts,0,0,730,730,platform"

Data anonymization and deletion

- Customer-requested deletion: follow documented erasure flow (ticket + verification) and confirm within 30 days for hosted customers.
- Backup deletion: backups/replicas honor the same deletion timeline; stored snapshots are tagged and purged per retention windows.

4) Secure SDLC

Gates and controls

- Design review: All major changes (network, auth, data-plane) require a Design Review ADR with security sign-off.
- Static analysis: All service code must pass SAST and dependency vulnerability scanning (failure threshold: no critical/high vulnerabilities untriaged).
- Secrets scanning: Prevent secrets in commits using pre-commit hooks and CI checks. Any leaked secret must be rotated within 1 hour of detection; incident ticket required.
- CI/CD pipeline protections: Signed build artifacts, reproducible builds, least privilege runners, and artifact provenance tracking.

Release checklist (must be completed before production rollout)

1. ADR approved and linked.
2. Threat model updated with new components.
3. SAST and dependency scans pass (or documented risk accepted).
4. Automated tests (unit/integration/e2e) meet coverage targets.
5. Rollout plan with rollback criteria and canary policy defined.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Detection and triage

- Detection sources: SIEM, IDS/IPS, guardrails from telemetry anomalies, user reports.
- Priority levels: P1 (active data exfiltration, service compromise), P2 (privilege misuse, suspected lateral movement), P3 (information disclosure of low-sensitivity data).

Immediate containment steps (for P1/P2)

1. Activate Security Incident Response (SIR) channel and notify exec stakeholders.
2. Snapshot affected hosts, revoke compromised credentials/tokens, and isolate affected network segments.
3. Preserve audit logs and evidence (copy to WORM storage, take hash).

Evidence collection and preservation

- Follow strict evidence chain-of-custody: record collector, timestamps, hashes, and storage location in the incident ticket.
- Capture: process memory dump (if relevant), disk snapshot, network flow logs, and relevant app logs.
- Do not perform destructive remediation before capture unless active containment requires it.

Post-incident activities

- Postmortem within 7 business days: root cause analysis, timeline, mitigations, and preventive actions.
- Lessons learned: incorporate into SDLC gates and monitoring.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Evidence sourcing and ownership

- Evidence types: architecture diagrams, IAM role membership exports, audit log extracts, change approvals, test artifacts, vulnerability scan reports, and control mappings.
- Evidence owners: engineering teams produce technical evidence; security curates and signs off for audits.

Standard evidence workflow

1. Audit request received (internal/external).
2. Security triages scope and assigns evidence owners.
3. Evidence is collected, labeled with control IDs, and uploaded to the evidence repository (WORM).
4. Security performs pre-audit review and flags gaps.

SLAs and traceability

- Internal evidence requests: 5 business days standard SLA.
- External (regulatory) audit requests: 10 business days SLA for initial package; expedited handling for contractual audits.
- All evidence items must include: owner, collection timestamp, related control ID, storage path, and checksum.

Audit readiness checklist (short)

- Up-to-date architecture diagrams and data flow maps.
- IAM role & membership exports for the last 12 months.
- Retention policy artifacts for logs and backups.
- Recent penetration test and remediation status.
- Incident log with summaries and corrective actions for the past 12 months.

7) Risk and Exceptions

Risk assessment and acceptance

- New risks are logged in the risk register with severity (low/medium/high) and mitigation plan.
- Security council evaluates high/critical risks weekly.

Exception process (when controls cannot be fully met)

1. Submit exception request via the exceptions form. Include: scope, justification, compensating controls, duration, and rollback plan.
2. Security reviews and assigns temporary risk rating.

3. Exceptions for high-risk controls require executive approval and a documented mitigation roadmap.
4. All exceptions are time-bounded (max 90 days) and reviewed monthly.

Template (one-line)

"exception_title,requestor,control_id,justification,compensating_controls,approved_by,expires_on"

8) Appendix and References

- Example CLI to export role membership (pseudo):

$ rdc iam export-roles --env prod --output roles-2026-03-01.csv

- Evidence repository location: s3://redwood-evidence-prod/worm/ (access restricted to security and audit roles)
- Key references: security playbook, RBAC policy ADR, audit logging spec, secure-sdlc-guide.
